desc:
Count the non-empty contiguous subarrays of nums whose sum is an odd number. Subarrays at different positions count separately, even if they hold the same values.

nums = [1, 3, 5]
odd sums: [1], [3], [5], [1, 3, 5]   (the sums 1, 3, 5 and 9)
result = 4
constraints: The answer is at most n(n + 1) / 2, which fits in a 32-bit integer
hints: Only the parity (even or odd) of each sum matters, so you never need the real values.
A subarray between prefix positions i < j has an odd sum exactly when the prefix sums at i and j have different parities.
Count how many earlier prefix sums (including the empty prefix) are even and how many are odd. For each new prefix, add the count of the opposite parity.
editorial: Let P_j be the parity of the sum of the first j elements, with P_0 = even. The subarray ending at position j and starting after prefix i has sum P_j - P_i, which is odd precisely when the two parities differ.

So sweep the array, keep how many earlier prefixes were even and how many odd (initially one even, the empty prefix), flip the current parity when you meet an odd element, and add the number of earlier prefixes with the opposite parity to the answer. That is O(n) time with O(1) space. Negative numbers work with x % 2 in Python, which returns 0 or 1.
